label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 4 uses a 5 by 8 irregular chart with per-run reversed counts, no hit-orientation feedback, touching vessels, no holes, fleet lengths 3, 3, and 2, and two sweep charges.
Simplified interaction exposes explicit band, block, and count buttons, including the star sweep count, followed by a Fire button.
The visible task shows the chart, block-direction arrows, persistent miss/hit/sunk marks, the vessel manifest, and remaining sweep charges; End Attempt/Certify is administrative.
The environment declares mouse and keyboard action surfaces, but this mechanic implements the task controls as mouse-click buttons.
autonomous_processes: None during idle intervals: the chart, selectors, hit marks, fleet state, sweep count, and terminal state do not change without an input handler running.
Certification can receive a response and issue a fresh chart after an explicit End Attempt click, but that is action-triggered administrative handling rather than autonomous task evolution.
grouped_control_modes: Simplified value-button selection for the band axis.
Simplified value-button selection for the block axis.
Simplified value-button selection for the count axis, including the star sweep.
Simplified Fire submissions of the currently selected band/block/count designation; a star submission sweeps one run and consumes a charge.
End Attempt/Certify is not an outcome-affecting control mode and is excluded from the real-time D witness.

clause_i.reason: For the adaptive search mode, an observation-free q cannot generally choose the best next designation from only its own action trace: identical prior actions can lead to different visible hit, miss, and sunk marks and therefore different candidate-vessel distributions.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded current screenshot is sufficient for the static search because it contains the chart geometry, visible direction arrows, persistent shot marks, remaining fleet lengths, and sweep count. A screenshot policy can enumerate compatible straight vessels and choose the next designation; no multi-frame temporal evidence is needed.

clause_iii.reason: There is no autonomous non-clock task-state evolution between outcome-affecting actions. Selector changes and Fire feedback are synchronous handlers, and the mechanic has no timer, requestAnimationFrame loop, physics update, or CSS animation. Consequently, for any Delta greater than zero while success remains possible, an available designation does not become unavailable or strictly less effective merely by waiting.

common_visible_process: None. The only visible chart evolution is synchronous feedback after Fire, or a new chart following an explicit failed certification; no autonomous visible process can witness clauses (i), (ii), and (iii) together.

pre_run.reason: The mathematical definition already yields No through clause (iii), so the pre-run override cannot change the label and no pre-run rate is required.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 4 activates the 5 by 8 irregular, reverse-count, orientation-hidden, touching-vessel profile with fleet lengths 3, 3, 2 and two sweeps.
Simplified mode is explicit band/block/count button selection followed by Fire; the configured observation window is 0 ms with one frame and the play allowance is 600 seconds.
The supplied control condition overrides the baseline parameters, and the seeded random generator creates the chart and fleet from a fixed seed rather than advancing an idle process.
The generator constructs static chart cells and runs, including local reverse-count directions and cell designations.
The fleet is placed once during generation, with touching allowed for difficulty 4; no movement or idle update is defined.
Simplified mode renders explicit selector buttons and binds them to synchronous selection updates.
The chart renders persistent visible shot classes and the local block arrows; the visible feedback is accumulated state, not an idle animation.
Fire synchronously resolves the selected designation, updates seen/hit/sunk/sweep state, and redraws the board.
Certification is an explicit fetch-driven action; an incomplete certification may receive a new chart, rather than the chart changing autonomously while idle.
The mechanic stylesheet contains presentation rules only and no animation or transition that changes task state during an idle interval.
The grader replays selector and Fire events synchronously from the event tape and computes pass/score from the resulting static seen and sunk sets; it has no time-dependent grading rule.
The verifier loads the exported result and invokes the independent designation replay grader; no autonomous or timing condition is added by verification.
The structural solver reads rendered cell classes and fleet-manifest status, enumerates compatible straight-vessel candidates, and fires adaptive designations from persistent visible marks.
